slides.label: Verse 2
lines: TOPIC: The Remarkable Death Of Jesus (Rhapsody of Realities 16 July 2025)

slides.label: Verse 3
lines: And when the centurion, which stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God (Mark 15:39).

slides.label: Verse 4
lines: Rhapsody Of Realities For Today’s MESSAGE:

slides.label: Verse 5
lines: The death of Jesus was extraordinary and filled with supernatural events that also confirmed His deity. After being falsely accused, arrested, and crucified, Jesus hung on the Cross while the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him (Matthew 27:42-43).

slides.label: Verse 6
lines: Even the two thieves crucified alongside Him joined in the mockery (Matthew 27:44, Mark 15:32).

slides.label: Verse 7
lines: Then, from the sixth hour (noon) to the ninth hour (3 p.m.), darkness covered the whole earth. This supernatural darkness lasted for three hours, signifying something beyond the natural realm.

slides.label: Verse 8
lines: At about the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” which means, “…My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46).

slides.label: Verse 9
lines: This was the moment when the sins of the whole world were laid upon Jesus. The Father, who is too holy to behold sin (Habakkuk 1:13), turned His back, and Jesus, who had never been separated from the Father, cried out in anguish.

slides.label: Verse 10
lines: This separation was the cup Jesus prayed about in the Garden of Gethsemane when He said, “…O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me…” (Matthew 26:39).

slides.label: Verse 11
lines: It was not death He dreaded but separation from the Father, which was a result of Him becoming sin for humanity. The Bible says, “For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him” (2 Corinthians 5:21).

slides.label: Verse 12
lines: Then, with a loud voice, He said, “…Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit…” (Luke 23:46).

slides.label: Verse 13
lines: Jesus commanded His own death. He consciously and deliberately handed over His spirit to the Father. Jesus had earlier declared, “Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again…I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again…” (John 10:17-18).

slides.label: Verse 14
lines: When Jesus yielded up the ghost, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, signifying the removal of the barrier between God and humanity, granting us access to the Father’s presence.

slides.label: Verse 15
lines: Even the centurion overseeing the crucifixion, upon witnessing how Jesus died, declared, “…Truly this man was the Son of God” (Mark 15:39).

slides.label: Verse 16
lines: The manner of His death testified of His divinity. Jesus’ death was no ordinary death. It was the ultimate sacrifice that brought salvation to all mankind.

slides.label: Verse 18
lines: Dear Father, thank you for the death of Jesus whose blood was the propitiation for sins. I rejoice in the finished work of Christ, knowing that He laid down His life for me and took it up again in victory. I live triumphantly, enjoying the benefits of His sacrificial love, now and always. Amen.
